Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (countdown for-loop with the `(uint)bool * -N + M` direction idiom — Watcom's REP MOVSD lowering fingerprint). Replace the whole loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * stride) or a struct assignment in a .keep.

Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `this_ptr_00` self-updates by self-indexing a constant element step, dereferencing a sibling array field (which decays to a pointer), then adding a constant; the sum equals the larger struct stride being walked. Replace `this_ptr_00->field` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar12` self-updates via element-arithmetic `(int)(pCVar12 + N) + M`, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar12) + M` equals the larger struct stride being walked (the pointer is typed to a sub-element). Replace `pCVar12->field` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
